address: 14944 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065
profile.reading:
This building is SLC2, one of five data centers DataBank operates on its Granite Point Campus in Bluffdale, Utah, roughly 20 miles south of Salt Lake City in the Salt Lake Valley. DataBank's own campus page places SLC2 at 14944 S Pony Express Road, Bluffdale, UT 84065, with 43,820 square feet of IT space and 3.25 megawatts of critical IT load, built to a 2N power and N+1 cooling design. DataBank acquired the underlying Granite Point site from C7 Data Centers in 2017; the campus previously operated under C7's branding before DataBank's takeover. Across the full five-building campus, DataBank states a combined 257,770 square feet of IT space and roughly 45.9 megawatts of critical IT load on about 23 acres, fed by diverse A and B power feeds from Rocky Mountain Power in an N+1 substation configuration. DataBank's campus materials list FISMA, SSAE 18, HIPAA/HITECH, PCI, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications applicable across the site, though no individual building page states a formal Uptime Institute Tier rating; a third-party aggregator separately claims a Tier III design standard for a neighboring building on the same campus, a claim DataBank's own materials do not repeat, so it is not applied here. Utah's "Silicon Slopes" technology corridor has grown substantially around Salt Lake County and Utah County over the past decade, drawing data center, software, and financial-technology employers, and Bluffdale's industrial-zoned land along the Pony Express Road corridor has become a recognized data center cluster alongside DataBank's campus. DataBank does not publish a specific year-opened date for SLC2 on its current site; SLC6, the newest of the five buildings, opened in 2023, which places SLC2 as an earlier phase of the same multi-building buildout.

Rocky Mountain Power filed for what it described as Utah's first major large-load energy agreement under the state's 2025 large-load legislation in early February 2026, an "Operation Gigawatt" filing with the Utah Public Service Commission covering a data center customer that agreed to cover its own service costs; this filing does not name DataBank or the Granite Point campus specifically, so it is noted here only as regional grid-planning context, not as a confirmed connection to SLC2. Utah's broader "Silicon Slopes" branding effort has helped position the state as a lower-cost alternative to coastal data center markets for operators seeking reliable power and a business-friendly regulatory climate.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, Granite Point Campus SLC2, fetched this session, confirms the address already on file, 14944 S Pony Express Rd, Bluffdale, UT 84065, and states 3.25 MW of critical IT load and 43,820 IT square feet.

reading.body:
DataBank SLC2 in Bluffdale, Utah delivers 3.25 MW of critical IT load across 43,820 square feet, ranking fifth among eight published Utah facilities and contributing 6.3 percent of the state's 51.69 MW of disclosed capacity.

The facility's power density—approximately 74 watts per square foot—reflects a mixed-use colocation environment rather than a purpose-built AI training hall. At standard colocation density of 10 kW per rack, this supports roughly 325 racks. At AI training density of 40 kW per rack, it supports roughly 81 racks. These calculations rest on assumed density, not operator claims.

For AI workloads, 3.25 MW is adequate for inference clusters or smaller training runs but falls short of hyperscale AI training campus scale. The operator's public specification page does not disclose power headroom, remaining capacity, connectivity profile, or tenant composition, all material facts for assessing expansion potential or current AI usage. Utah's mapped footprint remains undercounted, with 21 total facilities but most publishing no capacity figures.
